<description>
### Issues in order of importance

#35829 made the fields of `HTTPRequest` & `HTTPRemoteClient` private, but still allows anyone with a reference to a request to update the internal state `enum`. https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35829#discussion_r3860447518

`HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequest()` only needs to be a `static` method in order to forward a `shared_ptr` of a client to a new request.

### Commits solving these issues in same order

* http: Remove `HTTPRequest::SetState()` and introduce `HTTPRequest::Load()` - Removes the ability for other classes to directly modify the request state.
* 2 refactors: Extract `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequestInternal()` from a combination of `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequest()` and `HTTPRemoteClient::ReadRequest()` (the latter is removed)
</description>

"Ralph" caught something that I think needs to be addressed: https://review.fish.foo/traces/36124-656ddb44ba0db001d503cce52db5ac6e6db897f1-890-2.html

Edge case:
1. `m_send_buffer` is full (for some reason), so `m_req` gets held back (throttled) and is not dispatched to a worker
2. `m_recv_buffer` is empty because client sent one request and its now in `m_req`
3. this returns early every I/O loop and `m_req` never(*) gets dispatched, even after the send buffer drains:
```cpp
std::unique_ptr<HTTPRequest> HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequestInternal()
{
    if (m_recv_buffer.empty()) return nullptr;
```

(*) = if the client sends more data it will unclog the jam because then `m_recv_buffer` won't be empty anymore.

Suggested fix from Claude: skip only the parsing when the buffer is empty, and start req_state from the request's current state. This way a `Complete` request still gets dispatched to a worker.
```cpp
  HTTPRequest::State req_state{m_req->GetState()};
  try {
      if (!m_recv_buffer.empty()) {
          LineReader reader(m_recv_buffer, MAX_HEADERS_SIZE);
          ...
      }
  }
```
